challenges.title: Continuous shift work and the 56-hour limit

items.title: Justifying the 56-hour exception correctly
items.text: For roles involving consecutive shift or rotation work, Art. 15 of Cabinet Resolution No. 1 of 2022 permits an average working week of up to 56 hours — a narrowly defined exception that must be justified, not a blanket licence.

items.title: Matching qualifications to every client
items.text: 24/7 care rotations often change the caregiver on duty — yet every visit still has to match the qualification and availability of the carer assigned.

items.title: Protecting sensitive patient data under the PDPL
items.text: The PDPL classifies biometric and health data as sensitive personal data — including when clocked via mobile time tracking during client visits.

solutions.title: How Klacks takes the load off home care in the UAE
solutions.subtitle: From a properly justified shift exception to on-premise data storage — everything works together.

items.title: Rounds automatically optimised
items.text: Klacks plans visit routes between clients so that journeys stay short and time windows are met.

items.title: The 56-hour average continuously visible
items.text: Klacks continuously totals weekly working hours and makes the average visible, so you can keep the exception under Art. 15 of Cabinet Resolution No. 1 of 2022 in view — instead of simply assuming it applies.

items.title: Qualifications factored in automatically
items.text: Every visit is only assigned to carers with the matching qualification — with no manual checking at all.

items.title: PDPL-compliant on-premise data storage
items.text: Klacks runs on your own infrastructure. Sensitive patient and time-tracking data never leaves your organisation — not even for the AI.

items.title: Klacksy schedules by voice
items.text: "Fill tomorrow's rounds" is all it takes. If someone calls in sick, Klacksy immediately suggests available cover with the right qualification.
